is one beat in the animation. Statements inside a frame either change the graph
shape (structural) or move data along it (flow).

frame setup { +node a "A" +node b "B" +edge a b }
frame "first request" { a -> b "hello" }
Names are unquoted identifiers or quoted strings (use quotes for spaces).

+node api "API"        # introduce node
-node api               # remove node
Each statement renders a circle that morphs out of the source, slides along the edge,
and morphs into the target. Consecutive tokens that chain (the
of the next) render as ONE continuously travelling dot — that's how requests
feel like one motion through a stack.

client -> api "GET"        # forward along +edge client api
client <- api "200 OK"     # reverse along the same edge
says "same edge, motion reversed" — it does
create a second edge. Use it for every response/reply that flows back.
